statement.p: Let \int_{0}^2 f(x) \, dx = -10, \quad \int_{0}^3 f(x) \, dx = -5, \quad \int_{0}^2 g(x) \, dx = -14, \quad \int_{2}^3 g(x) \, dx = 10, \quad
Use these values to evaluate the given definite integrals.
d) Find the value a such that \displaystyle \int_{0}^3 \left(a f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx = 0.

static.solution:
Solution:
a) \int_0^2 \left(f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx = \int_0^2 f(x) \, dx + \int_0^2 g(x) \, dx = -10 - 14 = -24.
b) First find the integral of g from 0 to 3. \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx = \int_0^2 g(x) \, dx + \int_2^3 g(x) \, dx = -14 + 10 = -4. Then \int_0^3 \left(f(x) - g(x)\right) \, dx = \int_0^3 f(x) \, dx - \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx = -5 + 4 = -1.
c) First find the integral of f from 2 to 3. \begin{array}{rcl} \displaystyle\int_0^3 f(x) \, dx \amp =\amp \displaystyle\int_0^2 f(x) \, dx + \int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \\ -5 \amp =\amp -10 + \displaystyle\int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \\ \displaystyle\int_2^3 f(x) \, dx \amp =\amp 5 \end{array} Then \int_{2}^3 \left(3f(x) + 2g(x)\right) \, dx = 3\int_{2}^3 f(x) \, dx + 2\int_{2}^3 g(x) \, dx = 3(5) + 2(10) = 35.
d) Substitute known values for the integrals. \begin{array}{rcl} \displaystyle \int_{0}^3 \left(a f(x) + g(x)\right) \, dx \amp =\amp 0 \\ a \displaystyle \int_0^3 f(x) \, dx + \int_0^3 g(x) \, dx \amp =\amp 0\\ a(-5) - 4 \amp =\amp \\ a \amp =\amp \frac{ + 4}{-5} \end{array}
